page.overview:
Who is Ar-Gimilzôr?

Ar-Gimilzôr was the twenty-third King of Númenor, succeeding his father Ar-Sakalthôr.

Ar-Gimilzôr's reign was a difficult time for the Faithful (Elendili), who called for the return of the Númenóreans to the ways of the Valar and the Elves, for during this time he persecuted them for their beliefs. Use of the Elvish languages was forbidden in Númenor by his order in SA 3110. He also neglected the White Tree and no longer made pilgrimage to the Hallow of Eru. In fact, he was so distrustful of the Faithful that he forced them to move from Andúnië to the eastern part of the island near Rómenna and watched them carefully.

Ar-Gimilzôr's wife, Inzilbêth, was secretly an Elf-friend, and she passed on her ways to their son, Tar-Palantir. She was the daughter of Lindórië, who was herself a descendant of Tar-Elendil, the fourth King of Númenor, and also of Tar-Calmacil. Their second son, Gimilkhâd, opposed his elder brother's policies.

His chosen royal name (Ar-Gimilzôr) was Adûnaic. His Quenya, or 'regal', name was recorded in the Scroll of Kings as Tar-Telemnar ("Silver-flame"), a custom still observed out of superstition. Ar-Gimilzor's Adûnaic name translated is "Star-Flame".
